reason: The cited evidence (E1-E6) is entirely from a study on NbMoTaWSix, not TiVNbTa. It shows Si forms silicides and increases room-temperature strength and hardness in that system, but provides no data on high-temperature strength or oxidation resistance for TiVNbTa, nor does it support the claimed mechanism of solid solution strengthening and sluggish diffusion from Si addition.
premises: Si microalloying forms silicide phases in RHEAs
Silicide phases strengthen the matrix at high temperature
Solid solution strengthening and sluggish diffusion contribute to high-temperature strength
Optimal Si content exists for balancing strength and ductility
